result_changes.reason: CORP-2 (PMID 24694983) is now pooled from its own arm counts, 26/120 vs 51/120 (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.34-0.76), instead of the printed 'relative risk 0.49; 95% CI 0.24-0.65'. That figure is the relative risk REDUCTION: 1 - (0.51, 0.76, 0.34) = (0.49, 0.24, 0.66), printed under the label 'relative risk' in the same sentence as the counts. Mechanism: harness/design_key.ratio_label_audit (V1.0.1 acquisition cascade) -- a printed ratio outranks the same source's counts only if it agrees with them; a ratio that matches the 1-x reading with a flipped interval is refused as MISLABELLED_RRR. A ratio that fits neither reading is kept (it may be adjusted), not guessed. Trial membership is unchanged. The previously served result is superseded, not refuted: the numbers are not asserted wrong, and any trial set aside or not yet admitted stays eligible evidence awaiting adjudication.

certificate_scope.method: analysis_code_blobs is the static import closure (ast; module-level and function-local import statements, relative and absolute) of the roots, restricted to modules that resolve to a file under harness/ or scripts/. Nothing in the map is listed by hand. Values are Git SHA-1 blob identities: sha1('blob ' + len + NUL + bytes) over the file with CRLF normalised to LF, recomputable with `git hash-object -- <path>` at the anchoring commit.
certificate_scope.covers: 114 in-tree modules: the topic build (scripts/build_topic.py), the pipeline that computes every effect and its endpoint binding, the page and manuscript renderers, the two-limb publication gate, the canonical JSON and SHA-256 routines every digest in this certificate is computed with, this certificate builder, and the replay driver CI runs against it. A change of one byte in any of them moves analysis_code_sha256 and release_sha256.

not_covered.why: not reached from any root, so not part of building, rendering, gating or replaying this page: repository-level standard limbs run by scripts/verify_all.py on the whole tree (fix-state ledger, honest ratchet, held-out leak detector, served-artefact leak scan, search completeness), the search_v2 acquisition engine -- whose blob the search-completeness limb pins to the sealed measurement, not this certificate -- and adapters or stages outside the default build path. They are identified by the anchoring commit, not here.
not_covered.interpreter_and_packages: the Python interpreter, its standard library and third-party packages (scipy on the analysis path; openpyxl and sentence_transformers on optional paths) are not pinned by this certificate. Their effect is bounded by CI, which replays every page on a fresh install and refuses a byte difference; it is not bounded by a digest here.
not_covered.dynamic_imports: one dynamic import exists on the covered path (harness/acquisition.py resolves a source adapter by name for acquisition-time provenance); every adapter it can name lives under harness/ and is reached statically. importlib.metadata is queried for package versions only.
not_covered.data_read_by_code: the certificate pins code by blob and inputs by the other *_sha256 fields; a non-Python file under harness/ would be neither and is listed here if one exists.

certificate_scope.pins_bytes_not_self_reports: the map binds the BYTES of each module at the anchoring commit. It does not vouch for what any pinned component's own status fields say about themselves: a status value carried in the review or its cache (for example a span_location_check of OWED, or a REASON_TRUE on an absence row) is data recorded at build time and is covered as bytes by review_sha256 or extraction_objects_sha256, but this certificate does not assert that such a field is current, true of the implementation, or wired to code that enforces it. An OWED field can be stale in either direction. Whether a pinned check is in fact wired is established only by exercising the pinned bytes at the pinned commit, never by reading the field.
certificate_scope.how_to_use: bind a verdict to this certificate by release_sha256; check that analysis_code_blobs[path] equals `git hash-object -- path` at the commit you audited for every path you exercised, and that the path is in the map. A path missing from the map is a finding against the map, not a pass.

hash_inputs.protocol_sha: registration/build anchor Git commit (SHA-1, not a SHA-256 or prospective-registration claim)
hash_inputs.search_query_sha256: canonical ordered [{source_id, query}] from retrieval_ledger.json; query strings verbatim
hash_inputs.retrieval_ledger_sha256: canonical entire retrieval_ledger.json (including any raw-index digest)
hash_inputs.held_documents: SHA-256 of exact file bytes at each bundle-relative ref; all topic ft_*.txt/aact_*.json plus referenced held documents and source-manifest PDF/text pairs
hash_inputs.analysis_code_sha256: canonical analysis_code_blobs map; keys are the static import closure of certificate_scope.roots (harness.code_closure), values are Git SHA-1 blob identities of LF-normalized working source, declared root or optional module missing = NOT_PRESENT
hash_inputs.certificate_scope: prose and derived lists stating what analysis_code_blobs covers and what it does not; part of the certificate, so a change to the stated scope is a release change
hash_inputs.manuscript_sha256: UTF-8 bytes of harness.manuscript.render(review), including its reproduction context; the renderer's own bytes are pinned at analysis_code_blobs['harness/manuscript.py']
hash_inputs.release_sha256: canonical entire certificate excluding only release_sha256
